WANTED MAN - ANDREW PARSONS
(Nov 18th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is seeking the public’s assistance in locating wanted person Andrew Parsons of St. John’s.
Operational Patrol Services responded to a St. John’s residence for a report of an assault by the complainant’s former partner on Nov. 11.
The RNC’s Criminal Investigation Division was engaged and as a result of an investigation, Andrew Parsons, 51, is wanted and believed to be actively evading police.
Parsons, originally from Nova Scotia, is wanted on charges of assault, two counts of uttering threats, forcible confinement, assault causing bodily harm, and five counts of violence against an intimate partner.
Parsons is described to be 5’10” tall and 180 lbs with dark, greying hair. (See photo attached).
The RNC is asking anyone with information on his whereabouts to contact 709-729-8000.

MAN CHARGED WITH SEXUAL ASSAULT ON FLIGHT TO ST. JOHN’S
(Nov 18th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) has charged a 33-year-old Burin man with sexual assault following an incident aboard a flight destined for St. John’s.
The RNC received a report around 10 p.m. on Monday, November 17, regarding a sexual assault involving two passengers who were not known to one another.
Operational Patrol Services officers removed the male suspect from the plane and arrested him for sexual assault. He was held for court.
The RNC is encouraging all survivors of sexual violence to reach out to a trusted resource for support as soon as it is safe to do so.
Members of the RNC’s Child Abuse and Sexual Assault Unit are available to speak with anyone who has information or questions. Officers take a trauma-informed approach, providing education about legal and investigative options while directing survivors to appropriate resources based on their individual circumstances and needs.
The RNC can be reached at 709-729-8000. Anyone requiring immediate assistance is urged to call 911.

RNC URGES ONLINE SHOPPERS TO BE CAUTIOUS THIS HOLIDAY SEASON
(Nov 18th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is reminding online shoppers to exercise caution this holiday season, warning that fraudsters are looking to take advantage of shoppers through fake websites, misleading deals and phishing messages.
As people shop for the perfect gifts to put under the tree, scammers are creating fraudulent websites, advertising too-good-to-be-true deals, and sending convincing emails and text messages designed to steal personal and financial information.
The RNC is encouraging shoppers to take steps to protect their information and avoid falling victim to online fraud.
Police recommend buying only from trusted websites and verifying a retailer's authenticity. Shoppers are encouraged to type a retailer's web address directly into their browser rather than clicking on links.
Offers that appear too good to be true should also raise suspicion. Aggressive discounts, poorly designed websites and a lack of contact information may be warning signs of a fraudulent website.
The RNC also recommends making purchases using personal devices and secure networks rather than public Wi-Fi, keeping devices updated and maintaining active antivirus protection.
Shoppers are encouraged to protect their accounts by using strong, unique passwords and enabling multi-factor authentication where available.
The RNC further advises shoppers to monitor bank and credit card statements for unfamiliar charges, track deliveries and avoid leaving shipments unattended.
Anyone who suspects they have been a victim of fraudulent activity is encouraged to report it to the RNC at 709-729-8000 or the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre at 1-800-495-8501.

ALERT READY TEST TO TAKE PLACE THIS MORNING
(Nov 18th)

Residents may receive the test notification on their devices as part of the nationwide exercise.

THREE ARRESTED FOLLOWING BREAK-AND-ENTER AT FORMER WATERFORD HOSPITAL
(Nov 17th)
Three 18-year-old males have been arrested and charged following a break-and-enter at the former Waterford Hospital in St. John’s early Sunday morning, November 15th.
Shortly after midnight, officers with the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary’s (RNC) Operational Patrol Services and Police Dog Services were called to the scene.
When NFLD Bulletin arrived, officers had surrounded the former Administrative Building on the property.
In a response to NFLD Bulletin on Tuesday, November 17th, the RNC confirmed that three 18-year-old males were arrested at the scene.
All three were released to appear in court at a later date, each facing a single charge of break and enter.

MARYSTOWN JUNIOR FIREFIGHTER PROGRAM CELEBRATES 10TH ANNIVERSARY
(Nov 17th)
The Marystown Junior Firefighter Program is celebrating its 10th anniversary, marking a decade of providing young people with an opportunity to learn about firefighting and gain experience alongside members of the Fire Department.
Over the past 10 years, a total of 78 students have enrolled in the program, with several returning to take on additional responsibilities and some going on to serve in the fire service.
Of those students, 19 returned for a second year as Assistant Instructors, also known as Peer Leaders, while six returned for a third year in the same role.
Three former participants later returned to serve with the Marystown Fire Department, including Jayden, who is currently serving with the department as the program’s Committee Chairperson. Two other participants are serving or have served with neighbouring fire departments.
The 2026 Junior Firefighter Class recently wrapped up its 10-week program, with participants taking part in their final training session on the department’s training grounds before gathering for a banquet at the Fire Hall.
The final training session provided an opportunity for the students to put their learning into practice, with the department thanking its firefighters for providing instruction and oversight throughout the program.
The department extended its appreciation to the Town of Marystown, its firefighters, and the official sponsors who helped make the program possible, including Tina Belliveau (Co-operators), Coady’s Git er done LTD, Burin Peninsula Voice Against Violence, and Hickman Chevrolet Buick GMC Burin.
Additional thanks were extended to Adam’s Candy Sparkes for providing sweet treats, as well as Brushett’s Auto, Newco Metal & Auto Recycling Ltd. in Marystown, and Subway for their in-kind support and donations throughout the program.
With the 10th anniversary now celebrated, the department congratulated the 2026 Junior Firefighter Class and all former participants who have taken part over the years.
The program will welcome another group of students in 2027, with applications expected to open in late February.
/Info: Marystown Volunteer Fire Department.

YOUTH ARRESTED AFTER FLEEING POLICE AND CRASHING VEHICLE
(Nov 17th)
A youth is facing multiple Criminal Code charges after fleeing from an attempted traffic stop and crashing a vehicle in Harbour Grace Saturday night.
At approximately 10:30 p.m. on November 14, officers with the Trinity-Conception District RCMP were conducting proactive patrols on Harvey Street when they observed an oncoming vehicle travelling at 110 km/h in a posted 50 km/h zone.
Officers initiated a traffic stop, but the driver failed to comply and fled from police at a high rate of speed.
Officers conducted patrols in an effort to locate the vehicle and driver. Both were located a short time later at the scene of a single-vehicle crash.
The driver was not injured in the collision and was taken into custody without incident.
The youth faces charges of dangerous operation of a motor vehicle, flight from police and failure to comply with a probation order.
The youth was released from custody and is scheduled to appear in Harbour Grace Provincial Court at a later date.
Their driver’s licence was suspended, and the vehicle was seized by police and impounded.

THREE DRUG-IMPAIRED DRIVERS REMOVED FROM BURIN PENINSULA ROADS
(Nov 17th)
RCMP in Marystown say three drivers were removed from Burin Peninsula-area roads following separate drug-impaired driving investigations over the past week.
At approximately 9:00 p.m. on Tuesday, November 10, officers conducting proactive patrols stopped a vehicle on Mayor Avenue in St. Lawrence.
Police say the 21-year-old male driver showed signs of drug impairment and performed poorly during a roadside sobriety test. He was arrested for impaired operation and transported to the detachment, where he completed a Drug Recognition Evaluation and was provided with a demand for a bodily fluid sample.
On Sunday, November 15, shortly after 1:30 p.m., officers received a report of a suspected driver operating a vehicle while using cannabis.
The vehicle and driver were located on Route 210 near Winterland, where police initiated a traffic stop. The 35-year-old female driver was arrested for impaired driving and transported to the detachment for a Drug Recognition Evaluation. She was also provided with a demand for a sample to confirm impairment.
The third incident occurred shortly before 7:30 a.m. on Monday, November 16, when officers responded to a report of a possible impaired driver in Lewin’s Cove.
Police located and stopped the described vehicle. The 25-year-old male driver performed poorly during a Standardized Field Sobriety Test and was arrested for impaired operation. A search of the vehicle resulted in the location and seizure of a small quantity of illicit pills.
The driver was transported to the detachment, where he was assessed by a trained evaluator and provided with a demand for a sample to confirm drug impairment.
RCMP say laboratory testing results are pending in all three investigations to determine whether charges of impaired operation are appropriate.
The RCMP uses Standardized Field Sobriety Tests (SFSTs) at the roadside to provide preliminary indications of impairment, while Drug Recognition Evaluations (DREs) are conducted at police detachments by trained evaluators. These evaluations can include a demand for a bodily fluid sample and provide further evidence to support a drug-impaired driving charge.
Police remind motorists that operating a vehicle while under the influence of any drug, including legally purchased cannabis products, is against the law.
Anyone who suspects someone is driving while impaired by drugs or alcohol is asked to call 911 immediately.

FAMILY SEEKS COMMUNITY SUPPORT AFTER DEVASTATING HOUSE FIRE
(Nov 17th)
Five residents have been displaced and a family is asking for community support after a devastating house fire on Kelland Crescent in St. John’s claimed the life of a beloved family pet.
The fire occurred Friday afternoon, November 13th, at approximately 12:15 p.m., when firefighters with the St. John’s Regional Fire Department (SJRFD), along with personnel from the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) and NL Health Services, were dispatched to a reported vehicle fire at a residence.
While responding, emergency crews received updated information indicating that an electric scooter had caught fire inside the garage of the home.
Firefighters arrived within minutes to find an active fire in the garage, with thick smoke coming from the residence. Crews immediately deployed multiple attack lines and established a water supply before bringing the fire under control relatively quickly.
Speaking with NFLD Bulletin at the scene, SJRFD Platoon Chief Mike Hall confirmed that five residents had been displaced as a result of the fire. One pet was also found deceased.
The fire caused extensive damage to the garage, while the home sustained significant fire, smoke and water damage. No injuries were reported.
In a statement shared publicly by the family, they described November 13th, as every family’s worst nightmare, saying they lost everything in a matter of moments.
The family also shared the heartbreaking loss of their beloved cat, Loki, who they described as being like another child to the couple and another sibling to their three children.
The family says they are now taking things one day at a time while navigating the process of finding temporary housing and replacing basic necessities.
They are asking for support from the community, friends and kind strangers to help them get back on their feet.
Donations will go toward immediate necessities such as clothing, toiletries and groceries, temporary housing, and replacing furniture, household items and school supplies.
The family is also encouraging those unable to donate to share their fundraiser with others.
HOW TO HELP
Those wishing to support the family can visit GoFundMe and search for “Support Our Family after losinng everything in a house fire.” or visit our comment section and click the link we have attached. 
The family says every donation, regardless of size, as well as prayers, kind words and shares, are deeply appreciated as they begin the difficult process of rebuilding.

24-HOUR SNOW CLEARING TO RETURN TO NEWFOUNDLAND HIGHWAYS
(Nov 17th)
The Newfoundland and Labrador government says 24-hour snow clearing will return to selected highways, with additional details expected to be announced in the coming weeks.
Budget 2026 includes $3 million in funding to support the service and expand coverage to additional routes across the province.
Under the government’s currently published winter maintenance policy, seven-night overnight snow-clearing coverage is listed for the following routes:
METRO REGION;
- Outer Ring Road/Trans-Canada Highway (TCH), from Logy Bay Road to Foxtrap.
- Pitts Memorial Drive/CBS Bypass, from New Gower Street to Seal Cove.
- Team Gushue Highway, from the TCH to Topsail Road.
The policy also lists Sunday through Thursday overnight coverage for several other highways, including:
- Trans-Canada Highway, from Foxtrap to Whitbourne.
- Veterans Memorial Highway, from the TCH to Carbonear.
- Trans-Canada Highway, from Whitbourne to Clarenville.
- Trans-Canada Highway, from Gander to Grand Falls-Windsor.
- Botwood Highway, from the TCH to Botwood.
- Trans-Canada Highway, from Deer Lake to Stephenville’s Exit 3 at White’s Road.
- Route 430, from Deer Lake to Rocky Harbour, with the Gros Morne section maintained by Parks Canada.
- Lewin Parkway/Ring Road, Routes 450/450A.
- Route 460, from the TCH to Stephenville’s Cold Brook Depot.
Further details regarding additional routes and any changes to existing snow-clearing coverage are expected in the coming weeks.

WOMAN FACING MULTIPLE CHARGES FOLLOWING DISTURBANCE
(Nov 17th)
A 59-year-old woman is facing multiple charges following a disturbance at a residence near Thorburn Road in St. John’s Sunday evening.
At approximately 8:26 p.m. on November 16th, members of the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary’s (RNC) Operational Patrol Services responded to the residence.
During the course of the investigation, officers arrested a female for assault. While in custody, the woman began making threats toward police officers.
The 59-year-old woman was transported to the St. John’s lockup, where she was charged with assault, being unlawfully in a dwelling, and uttering threats.

WANTED MAN ARRESTED AT ST. CLARE’S HOSPITAL
(Nov 17th)
A 44-year-old man was arrested on an outstanding warrant following a disturbance in the parking lot of St. Clare’s Hospital in St. John’s Monday evening.
At approximately 7:10 p.m. on November 16th, members of the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary’s (RNC) Operational Patrol Services responded to a disturbance in the hospital parking lot.
Upon arrival, officers located an intoxicated male. Subsequent checks revealed that the man was wanted on an outstanding arrest warrant.
Police arrested the 44-year-old man and transported him to the St. John’s lockup.

75 YEAR OLD DECEASED AFTER BEING STRUCK BY VEHICLE
(Nov 17th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is investigating a fatal pedestrian-vehicle collision on Bay Bulls Road in St. John’s.
At approximately 4:30 p.m. Friday, November 13, officers with Operational Patrol Services and Accident Investigation responded to a report of a pedestrian-vehicle collision on Bay Bulls Road.
The pedestrian, a 75-year-old woman, succumbed to her injuries.
The driver of the vehicle was uninjured, co-operative with police and remained at the scene.
The investigation remains ongoing.
RNC Collision Reconstructionists are seeking witnesses or video footage, including CCTV, dash camera or cell phone video, from the area in the lead-up to or immediately following the collision.
Anyone with information is asked to contact the RNC at 709-729-8000.
The RNC has extended its sincere condolences to the family and friends of the deceased.

DRIVER FACING IMPAIRED DRIVING CHARGES IN MOUNT PEARL
(Nov 17th)
A 35-year-old man is facing impaired driving charges following a traffic stop on Mount Carson Avenue in Mount Pearl Monday afternoon.
At approximately 2:37 p.m. on November 16th, a member of the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary’s (RNC) Operational Patrol Services responded to a report of a possible impaired driver.
The officer conducted a traffic stop on the vehicle, and during the course of the investigation, the male driver was arrested for impaired driving.
The 35-year-old man was later released from custody with a future court date to answer to charges of impaired driving and driving with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg%.
Police impounded the vehicle and also issued summary offence tickets for driving while suspended, failing to transfer ownership of the vehicle, and having open alcohol in the vehicle.

SINGLE-VEHICLE ROLLOVER SLOWS TRAFFIC ON PITTS MEMORIAL DRIVE
(Nov 17th)
Emergency crews responded to a single-vehicle rollover on Pitts Memorial Drive in St. John’s Sunday afternoon, November 15th. 
At approximately 1:30 a.m., officers with the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) were attending the scene of the rollover in the eastbound lanes near the Kilbride overpass.
When NFLD Bulletin arrived at the scene, officers had one eastbound lane closed, resulting in slowed traffic through the area.
Paramedics with NL Health Services also responded and assessed at least one person at the scene.
There did not appear to be any serious injuries.

MAN CHARGED WITH COCAINE TRAFFICKING
(Nov 16th)
A 55-year-old Happy Valley-Goose Bay man is facing multiple charges following a traffic stop in Sheshatshiu that resulted in the seizure of a significant amount of currency, a weapon and other evidence consistent with drug trafficking activity.
At approximately 7:00 p.m. on Friday, November 13, Sheshatshiu RCMP stopped a vehicle on McKenzie Drive as part of an ongoing investigation led by the RCMP Labrador District General Investigation Section (GIS).
During the stop, officers located and seized a significant amount of currency, a weapon and other evidence consistent with drug trafficking activity.
The driver was identified as 55-year-old Paul Melville Vader of Happy Valley-Goose Bay. He was arrested and held in police custody before appearing in court over the weekend.
Vader was charged with trafficking in a controlled substance (cocaine), possession of property obtained by crime over $5,000, and failure to comply with the conditions of a Release Order.
He was remanded into custody and was expected to appear next in provincial court on Monday, November 16.
Five other occupants inside the vehicle were also arrested, identified and later released without charge.
The investigation remains ongoing, and additional charges are possible.
The RCMP notes that cocaine is the leading cause of overdose deaths in Newfoundland and Labrador. Police also remind the public that naloxone is ineffective in combatting cocaine overdoses. Anyone who suspects a person is experiencing a cocaine overdose should immediately seek medical attention.
Residents who suspect drug trafficking activity in their neighbourhood are encouraged to contact their local police detachment.
